title: 2026 iGEM Grand Jamboree

tracks.name: Measurement you can defend
tracks.line: Cheap instruments that produce numbers a judge will believe.
tracks.have: An OD600 channel on commodity photodiodes, a reference channel 32 counts wide at 0.067 OD per count, a DNPH activity assay at 7.25 mU/mL with two QC items still open, and a TiO₂ calibration from last August.
tracks.want: A defensible answer to what makes a home-built instrument's number admissible: which reference material, which raw data published, which error bars earned rather than assumed.

sessions.title: Fusing Living Biological Neurons with Silicon Chips
The Foundry Era: From Parts to Platforms
sessions.ask: What is the smallest useful automation unit for a team with no foundry, and what should they not try to automate?

sessions.title: Systematic assay design for resource-constrained projects
sessions.ask: What is the minimum you must characterise before a cheap assay's number is allowed into a figure?

tracks.name: The self-running experiment
tracks.line: Closed-loop control, the digital twin, and AI over process data.
tracks.have: A 434-hour run with two events found 26.7 h ahead of the operator, a green-light schedule chosen by Bayesian optimisation, and an invariant explorer whose fouling margin moved 0.26 → 0.73 on three corrections.
tracks.want: How people who sell autonomous labs handle a sensor artefact, because our own naive loop mistriggers on the 29 h OD dip that turned out 40% instrument.

sessions.title: The AI x Synthetic Biology Revolution
The Autonomous Lab: When Biology Runs Itself
sessions.ask: What does your trigger logic do with a sensor artefact? Ours put a 40% instrument drop into a real OD dip at 29 h.

sessions.title: Machine learning for the design and optimization of new biological sequences and networks
sessions.ask: How much wet-lab validation does a designed sequence need before you will put it in a figure?

sessions.title: Tools to Drive DBTL Efficiently, De-Risk Scale-Up, and Prioritize High-Quality Data
A Design Is Only a Prediction: Where AI Meets the Bench
sessions.ask: What do you report when the model and the bench disagree, and the bench is the one you cannot repeat?

tracks.name: Hosts that actually secrete
tracks.line: Non-model chassis, secretion, and the cell-free fallback.
tracks.have: A Level-2 construct read end to end twice and four blockers in front of it, the fourth being that secreting a PLP-dependent oligomeric ACC deaminase has no precedent anywhere.
tracks.want: The decision rule for when to stop engineering a signal peptide and change the strategy — and whether cell-free gets folded, active enzyme or merely protein.

sessions.title: Rebuilding Translation: The PURE System and Where Cell-Free Biology Goes Next
sessions.ask: For a PLP-dependent oligomeric enzyme, does cell-free get you folded, active protein — or just protein?

sessions.title: The Other 99%: Engineering Non-Model Organisms
sessions.ask: When a Gram-positive host will not secrete a heterologous enzyme, at what point do you stop engineering the signal peptide and change the host?

sessions.title: Bringing colours to life
sessions.ask: What did you have to give up about the plant to make the chemistry work at volume?

tracks.name: Parts other people can use
tracks.line: Standards, registry, machine-readable data, open science.
tracks.have: Four codon-optimised composites and four MD figure sets, a parts library verified against IDT, and a published BOM with a retired membrane part number still in it.
tracks.want: What makes a registration machine-readable rather than merely machine-visible, now that registries are being rebuilt for AI to read.

sessions.title: Standards in Synthetic Biology and the Role of iGEM
sessions.ask: For a cheap photodiode instrument, what makes a calibration credible to you — the reference material, or the published raw counts?

sessions.title: Open Infrastructure for AI-Native Synthetic Biology
sessions.ask: What in a part registration makes it machine-readable rather than merely machine-visible?

sessions.title: Git for Genomes
sessions.ask: What does the tool refuse to track, and where do teams still lose the provenance?

sessions.title: Publishing Interdisciplinary Research

tracks.name: Responsibility as design, not paperwork
tracks.line: Biocontainment, governance, dual use, and the public's voice.
tracks.have: A kill switch that is the weakest part of the design, and human practices built from interviews.
tracks.want: Governance practised rather than described — and what a 1976 citizens' committee asked that a modern IHP interview does not.

sessions.title: Welcome and Introductions
DNA Dilemmas: A Policy-Building Challenge
sessions.ask: Where does DNA synthesis screening actually fail — the order, the sequence, or the customer?

sessions.ask: What did the 1976 citizens' committee ask that a modern IHP interview does not?

sessions.ask: What should a small team be required to write down before it lets a model choose an experiment?

sessions.title: Governing the Future of Generative Biology
Global Efforts to Prevent Biological Misuse
Operation Outbreak: Advancing Preparedness Through Simulation
sessions.ask: What did the venue-wide data show that the participants did not notice themselves?

tracks.name: From project to product
tracks.line: Translation, funding, IP, and scale — whether a GEMS project outlives its competition year.
tracks.have: A bioreactor at Tier 2 of our own published audit, an industry report, and a cost claim the project brief forbids us to make.
tracks.want: What an investor, a technology-transfer office and a biomanufacturer each need to see before a school project becomes a thing that exists next year.

From Research to Impact: Building the Future of IP Transfer on Evidence

tracks.name: Why it didn't reproduce
tracks.line: Reproducibility and failure analysis as institutional memory.
tracks.have: Four formula errors in Experiment #9, a chlorophyll ratio range that cannot be believed, a 1.460× standard-concentration error in the first DNPH assay, and an OD dip that was 40% instrument.
tracks.want: A method for reading our own failures that is better than remembering them, and somewhere to put them where a judge finds them on purpose.

sessions.ask: Which promise in a student project should a judge refuse to reward?
